governance_context.executive_summary: Toptal will build the ARC application, one application within the client's larger genomics platform, and deliver QA test automation across four sequential milestones: P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, and P3 Launch. The stack includes a React/Next.js micro-frontend shell and ARC micro-frontend, FastAPI and nomenclature services, Snowflake, and Azure AD/MSAL, tested with Playwright, Jest, and Pytest. The client owns the platform infrastructure and data tier, including ingestion pipelines and the Snowflake data model.

charter.project_purpose: Build the ARC genomics application and automate its QA testing so scientists can search and visualize genomic association data within the client's platform.
delivery_objectives: Build the micro-frontend shell and ARC micro-frontend with faceted search, result detail, and haplotype visualization.
Build the FastAPI services (search, async processing, OneGWAS write integration) and the nomenclature service.
Deliver automated test scripts, execution, and defect reports for Toptal-built and designated client-built components.
Run UAT after each milestone, then harden, smoke test, and run a 48-hour defect watch at launch.
Produce training materials and user documentation.
success_criteria: Each milestone passes its acceptance gate with client sign-off.
Toptal-built components meet the stated latency and render-time targets (e.g., search P95 < 1s), unless telemetry attributes a miss to client-owned platform components.
For client-built components, test scripts are delivered and executed and a defect report is issued; achieving the targets is the client's responsibility.
No open critical defects in Toptal-built work at UAT exit, and all critical and high defects closed with a green full regression before cutover.
Production smoke tests pass 100% and the 48-hour defect watch is clean.
high_level_scope: P1 Foundation (weeks 1-6): micro-frontend shell, Azure AD/MSAL authentication, E2E test harness, pipeline quality gates, security testing, and validation of the data model and governance controls.

P2a Services and Data (weeks 7-16): FastAPI search and detail endpoints, async query processing, OneGWAS direct-write integration, performance spike, and validation of data ingestion, migration, extraction, and taxonomy.
P2b Application Surface (weeks 17-21): ARC micro-frontend search and results, detail view, haplotype features, nomenclature service, and related test suites.

P3 Launch (weeks 22-26): integration, performance, security, and cross-browser (Chrome and Edge) testing, test data, UAT, hardening, production smoke tests, MTA Store parity confirmation, and training documentation.
exclusions: Platform infrastructure, DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, security design, and architecture and design stories.
Snowflake data model design, data governance controls, and data ingestion and migration builds.
Integration test plan, UAT coordination and sign-off, go-live planning, production deployment, and decommission activities.
Hypercare and post-launch maintenance beyond the 48-hour defect watch.
Remediation of defects in client-built components and achievement of numeric targets for client-built work.
Creation, extension, or maintenance of the client's design system.

decisions.decision_text: Work is delivered through four sequential milestones that act as acceptance gates: P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, and P3 Launch.
decisions.rationale: Sequential gates ensure each milestone is accepted before the next begins, with UAT after each one.

decisions.decision_text: Estimated schedule is 26 weeks from the start date: P1 weeks 1-6, P2a weeks 7-16, P2b weeks 17-21, P3 weeks 22-26.
decisions.rationale: Provides the agreed baseline timeline, assuming no holiday breaks or stoppages.

source_reference.clause_or_slide: Section 4 Work Output; Section 7 Assumptions & Dependencies

decisions.decision_text: Toptal owns ARC application development (micro-frontend shell, ARC micro-frontend, FastAPI services, nomenclature service) and QA test automation; Client owns the platform layer and data tier.
decisions.rationale: Clear ownership boundaries separate Toptal-built work from Client-built components.

decisions.decision_text: Work follows SAFe-aligned methodology and terminology; industry-standard definitions apply where SAFe is silent.
decisions.rationale: Ensures a shared vocabulary for agile terms such as epic, feature, and backlog.

decisions.decision_text: QA is delivered as automated test scripts, their execution, and defect reports rather than manual QA passes, and testing covers the full platform including SSO and external integrations.
decisions.rationale: Testing ARC requires validation against the full platform, and automation provides repeatable results.

source_reference.clause_or_slide: Section 3 Quality Assurance and Test Automation

decisions.decision_text: For Client-built components marked 'Certification', Toptal delivers test scripts, execution, and a defect report; achieving the target and remediating failures is Client's responsibility.
decisions.rationale: Toptal does not control Client-built components, so acceptance depends on testing delivery rather than target achievement.

source_reference.clause_or_slide: Section 3 Quality Assurance and Test Automation; Section 4 Work Output

decisions.decision_text: If telemetry shows a missed latency target is caused by a Client-owned platform component, the criterion is treated as met for Toptal's work and logged in the defect report for Client remediation.
decisions.rationale: Toptal-built components run on Client-owned platform components (e.g., Snowflake, Azure AD, CloudFront) that affect latency.

decisions.decision_text: UAT runs after each milestone and is limited to two runs per milestone within the fixed price; additional runs are handled by Change Order.
decisions.rationale: Caps UAT effort to protect the fixed price and schedule.

decisions.decision_text: Re-testing after Client remediation of failed Certification targets is included once; additional re-runs and rework from upstream changes (e.g., Snowflake schema or taxonomy shifts) are handled by Change Order.
decisions.rationale: Controls scope for test cycles driven by factors outside Toptal's control.

source_reference.clause_or_slide: Section 3 Quality Assurance and Test Automation; Section 7 Assumptions & Dependencies

decisions.decision_text: Toptal will use Client's existing design system for all user-facing screens; creating, extending, or maintaining it is excluded, and additional components or changes are handled by Change Order.
decisions.rationale: Keeps design system ownership with the Client and limits scope to ARC-specific components.

decisions.decision_text: The Cogen API is assumed to be about 95% available and stable; test failures and re-tests from lower availability are handled by Change Order.
decisions.rationale: Cogen availability is outside Toptal's control and could otherwise cause unplanned test effort.

decisions.decision_text: Governance cadence: Day 1 kickoff, biweekly sprint demos, joining Client daily standups, ad-hoc working sessions, and a milestone acceptance review at each milestone end.

commercial_guardrails.contract_type_implication: Fixed Bid: fixed fees are tied to four sequential milestones (P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, P3 Launch). Anything beyond the defined Work Output needs a Change Order, or margin is absorbed.
commercial_guardrails.billing_consumption_assumption: Fees are fixed per milestone, not timesheet-driven, and the Weekly Status Report includes a milestone billing snapshot. Milestones are accepted sequentially, with Client sign-off at each gate.
commercial_guardrails.staffing_assumption: The schedule (26 weeks: P1 wks 1-6, P2a wks 7-16, P2b wks 17-21, P3 wks 22-26) assumes no holiday stoppages. It also assumes Client-built work is finished, and domain users, domain experts, scientist UAT groups and the IdP team are available, before dependent Toptal work starts. Toptal staff join Client's daily standups.
commercial_guardrails.commercial_exposure_note: Margin is exposed to Client-side delays, to UAT beyond two runs per milestone, and to re-test cycles beyond those allowed. Further exposure comes from Cogen API availability below ~95%, upstream Snowflake schema or taxonomy changes, design-system changes, and ARC-specific components beyond the estimated number. Fixing defects in Client-built components is Client's responsibility, and Certification targets are not a condition of Toptal's acceptance.
commercial_guardrails.approved_work_rule: Only the Toptal-built Work Output listed per milestone, plus test scripts, execution and defect reports for the Client-built components marked Certification, is authorized. Approved Change Orders are also authorized.
commercial_guardrails.non_approved_work_rule: Do not perform out-of-scope work without a written Change Order. This includes fixing defects in Client-built components, platform/DevOps, design-system work, and data ingestion or migration builds. It also includes testing other Client-built components, extra test re-runs, extra UAT runs, and hypercare beyond the 48-hour defect watch.
commercial_guardrails.work_at_risk_rule: No work-at-risk is pre-approved. Starting work before Client dependencies are complete, or beyond approved scope or budget, requires written PMO Lead approval and executive exception sign-off.
commercial_guardrails.change_control_trigger: A Change Order is required for UAT beyond two runs per milestone, additional re-test runs, and Cogen availability below ~95% causing re-tests. It is also required for upstream Snowflake schema or taxonomy changes causing test rework, design-system changes or extra components, and added testing of other Client-built components. Any material scope shift, timeline variance over 5 days, or budget variance over 10% also triggers one.
commercial_guardrails.change_order_route: PMO Lead leads -> DM aligns client -> Client approves -> Contracting issues change order
commercial_guardrails.budget_baseline: [CONFIRMATION REQUIRED] Fixed price split across four milestones over an estimated 26 weeks; the monetary amount is not stated.
commercial_guardrails.variance_indicator: Green (<5% variance); no variance reported at baseline.
commercial_guardrails.escalation_threshold: Budget burn rate exceeding weekly cap by >10%, or any Client dependency delay that threatens a milestone start date.

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Exhibit A, Overview: milestones are 'P1 Foundation, P2a, P2b, P3 Launch'. Work Output table numbers them 'Milestone 1-4' (P2b = Milestone 3, P3 = Milestone 4). Client Responsibilities: 'UI/UX designs for the Milestone 3 screens'.
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: Mixed P-labels and Milestone numbers can cause the wrong milestone to be read for design delivery, billing and sign-off timing.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Please confirm the single milestone naming convention, and confirm that 'Milestone 3 screens' means the P2b Application Surface screens and the date the UI/UX designs are due.

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Assumptions: 'Estimates include integrating it and building up to [N] ARC-specific components... Further components or changes are addressed by Change Order.'
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: The component cap is an unfilled placeholder, so the Change Order trigger for design-system components cannot be enforced. This creates margin and scope-creep risk on the P2b UI build.

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Assumptions: 'The Cogen API is assumed to be available and stable at approximately 95%, as assessed by Syngenta. Test failures and re-test cycles arising from Cogen availability below that level will be addressed by Change Order.'
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: 'Approximately 95%' has no measurement window or method, and the assessor is not defined as a role or process. Disputes over what triggers a Change Order could cause unfunded re-testing.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Please define the Cogen availability metric (measurement period, method, tool) and who records the measurement that triggers a Change Order.

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Assumptions: 'The external API integrations within scope are Cogen and Tagasys.' Third Party Items: 'Cogen and Tagasys APIs... Provided by Client during the engagement. [confirm]'. The Work Output table has no story for Cogen or Tagasys.
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: The integrations are called in scope, but no build or test deliverable, acceptance criteria or confirmed provider exists. This leaves the scope boundary and test effort undefined.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Please confirm whether Cogen and Tagasys integration build is in Toptal's scope or only testing, which stories cover them, and who provides the API access and credentials.
